claim_boundary: This protocol tests two supervised transfer decisions in the tiny synthetic MLX fixture. Even a passed gate would justify only iteration to a separate full V2; it cannot establish return-A behavior, unlabeled wake, physical-memory conservation, large-model behavior, compute efficiency, or Pop's theorem.

decision.scope: horizon-3 exhaustive shadow rollout as the V2 directional controller
decision.surviving_signal: controlled partial evidence that supervised task-conditioned direction can beat static, fixed random, and a wrong-task rollout across two transfers
decision.reentry_condition: a qualitatively different controller must produce a complete finite matrix and beat exact one-step, fixed random, and future-aware fixed split on untouched seeds

reproduction.result: protocol, trajectory, summary CSV/JSON, diagnostics, and interpretation reproduced byte-for-byte
reproduction.seed26_failure_repeat: b_exact_one_step again produced non-finite training gradients
